name: Nginx-Proxy-Manager-MCP
description: MCP server for Nginx Proxy Manager - manage your reverse proxy through AI assistants. This container exposes an MCP (Model Context Protocol) endpoint on port 8000 that AI assistants can use to manage your Nginx Proxy Manager instance: list proxy hosts, create/update/delete hosts, manage SSL certificates, check system health and more. It has no web interface - connect to it from an MCP client (e.g. Claude Desktop, Cursor, or any MCP-compatible agent) using the HTTP transport: http://YOUR-Unraid-IP:8000/mcp Before Installing: 1. Make sure you have Nginx Proxy Manager running and note its API URL (http://NPM-IP:81/api) 2. Create an NPM user or use an existing admin account (email + password) 3. Optional: enable the destructive tools (create/update/delete) by setting NPM_MCP_ENABLE_DESTRUCTIVE_TOOLS=true 4. Optional: set NPM_MCP_AUTH_TOKEN to require a bearer token for MCP clients For log access (get_proxy_host_logs tool), mount your NPM data directory read-only and set NPM_LOG_DIR accordingly - see the project documentation for details.

paths.name: NPM Logs
paths.description: Optional: mount NPM's log directory here (read-only) and set NPM Log Dir to /data/npm-logs

ports.name: MCP Port
ports.description: MCP server port (HTTP transport). Connect MCP clients to http://YOUR-UNRAID-IP:8000/mcp

variables.name: NPM API URL
variables.description: Nginx Proxy Manager API endpoint, e.g. http://192.168.1.10:81/api

variables.name: Enable Destructive Tools
variables.description: Enable write/destructive tools (create, update, delete, enable, disable). Leave false for read-only access.

variables.name: MCP Auth Token
variables.description: Optional: bearer token required for MCP HTTP clients. Generate one with: openssl rand -hex 32

variables.name: MCP Transport
variables.description: Transport mode: http (default, for remote agents) or stdio

variables.name: NPM Log Dir
variables.description: Optional: path to mounted NPM log directory (enables get_proxy_host_logs). Mount NPM's /data/logs read-only and point this at the mount path.
